name: GitHub
comments: Estimated per active repository for storage and CI/CD, based on GitHub's sustainability reporting.
calculation_notes: Conservative proxy: ~5 g CO2/month and ~0.1 kWh/month per active repository, covering storage and CI/CD.
GitHub runs on Azure with renewable energy commitments (GitHub sustainability blog).
Monthly rates cover 20 working days; co2.ts prorates them over the report's duration_days (working days).

name: S3 / Static Hosting
description: Asset storage and static file hosting, for demo and staging environments only.
comments: Based on the data transferred each month by demo and staging environments, converted with a per-gigabyte carbon factor.
calculation_notes: ~8 GB transferred per month by demo and staging environments x ~0.001 kg CO2/GB = ~8 g CO2/month.
Energy estimate: ~0.5 kWh/month.
The per-GB factor is linked to the Green Web Foundation; its exact origin is not documented.
Monthly rates cover 20 working days; co2.ts prorates them over the report's duration_days (working days).

name: Claude Code (AI)
description: Occasional AI assistance for tools, CI/CD scripts or documentation.
comments: Based on my own Claude Code logs for occasional use (real request and token counts), converted to energy with TokenAtlas estimates drawn from published research.
calculation_notes: Energy per request: 5 Wh, measured on the capveggie-mijote-platform project over 28 working days (6 weeks ending 2026-10-20): 11,112 requests, 2.58 billion tokens (98.5% cache reads), 55.9 kWh.
Excluded days: 2026-10-08 (multi-session security review) and 2026-10-19 (production setup with continuous log reading).
Tokens read from local Claude Code transcripts (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl), deduplicated by message id and request id.
Energy per million tokens (TokenAtlas mid estimates, GPU compute only): 390 Wh input, 1,400 Wh output, 490 Wh cache write, 15 Wh cache read.
Model mix: 70% Opus, 30% Sonnet, Sonnet weighted at 0.6x Opus (TokenAtlas tiers), so a 0.88 factor.
Simon Couch's constants (1,950 Wh output, 39 Wh cache read) give about twice as much; Zeke Hausfather measured about 3 kWh per active day for similar volumes.
Datacenter overhead (cooling, network, CPU) is not included; TokenAtlas suggests 1.5x to 3x.
Grid: 341 gCO2e/kWh, US average (eGRID 2024), as used by Zeke Hausfather. Anthropic does not publish where requests are served.
Agentic requests carry long contexts, so the 5 Wh figure is likely an upper bound for lighter use. Older usage (before 2026) had context windows about 4x smaller.
Monthly rates cover 20 working days; co2.ts prorates them over the report's duration_days (working days).
Light use: ~4 requests per working day x 20 days x 5 Wh = 0.4 kWh/month; x 341 g = 136 g CO2/month.

name: Gmail (Google Workspace)
comments: Counted from my sent mail as a yearly average, with a per-email carbon estimate.
calculation_notes: ~40 sent emails per 20 working days (~2 per day), yearly average of the actual sent mail count.
40 emails x 0.3 g CO2/email = 12 g CO2/month. The 0.3 g factor is a commonly cited figure; its origin is not documented here.
Energy: ~0.001 kWh/email, so 0.04 kWh/month.
Google no longer claims operational carbon neutrality since 2023 (2024 environmental report).
Monthly rates cover 20 working days; co2.ts prorates them over the report's duration_days (working days).
